**[P1] A backward clock adjustment can reopen an exhausted elapsed allowance.**  
Location: [runAdmission.ts:207](</Users/pmark/.codex/worktrees/0c59/arcadia/src/scout/runAdmission.ts:207>), particularly lines 207–220 and transactional rollback in `withHistory`.

`lastClock` advances only on successful operations. A refusal at the 90-minute elapsed limit throws and retains the earlier timestamp. A subsequent backward clock adjustment that remains later than that timestamp passes rollback detection and admits another attempt.

Independent synthetic reproduction:

```text
First reservation: 09:00:00; failure recorded: 09:00:01
At +91m: refused — elapsed allowance exhausted
Persisted lastClock after refusal: 09:00:01
Clock adjusted backward to +2m: ADMITTED attempt 2, repairs 1
```

The retry supplied changed source, distinct review/QA identities, and freshly pinned synthetic evidence. Neither history nor its freshness digest was restored. This violates criteria 2 and 3: elapsed time includes waits, and clock rollback must refuse admission.

Reproduction: [admission-review-clock.mts](/private/tmp/admission-review-clock.mts). Executed against the verified candidate modules using:

```sh
node --import /Users/pmark/.codex/worktrees/0c59/arcadia/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /private/tmp/admission-review-clock.mts
```

Exit **0**, demonstrating the defect; Node **v22.23.1**, zero provider calls. The initial `mise exec` invocation exited **1** because its trust-link write was denied; direct Node execution followed the existing Notes remedy.

The actual clock boundary is trusted `Date.now()` plus a persisted high-water timestamp from successful operations. It detects rollback below that timestamp; it cannot detect every backward adjustment across waits/restarts. Persisting failed observations would address the demonstrated reopening, but the broader elapsed-time guarantee also needs an explicit clock-continuity assumption or evidence.
